speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Family and Social Development)
text: Applicants who file maintenance applications have to attend mediation before their case is heard by the Tribunal.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: First, I would like to declare that I am a mediator with the Tribunal for the Maintenance of Parents (TMP).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Also, if the Senior Parliamentary Secretary could give comments on the effectiveness of the process in place, including mediation, in resolving the issues raised at TMP.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Further, whether there is any scope of review of the role of TMP, perhaps in providing and enhancing services to the families, for example, in counselling or allowing for financial planning classes for the families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Looking at the details and numbers, as I had said earlier, we cannot see any trend.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, from 2013 to 2017, numbers have gone down.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, as a whole, we feel that the Commissioner for the Maintenance of Parents (CMP) has been able to help in facilitating to resolve the issues amicably.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We feel that this can be attributed largely to the CMP's success in resolving maintenance disputes through conciliation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We feel that with better upfront conciliation, fewer applications are being filed at TMP.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is not only about conciliation or about how we can help them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If along the way, we find that there are efforts that we can carry out at the Social Service Offices level by community agencies, we will do our best to refer.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to promote filial piety; we want families to be able to support one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And the community can play a part in this.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What I would like to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary is whether, given that these are encouraging results and, indeed, we want more conciliations rather than going through the Tribunal per se, that more efforts, more focus, even more attention and more publicity be given.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We do know that there are strains for many families in this day and age, and every family that we can help, first publicise this avenue and how conciliations can result in success.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I will urge the Ministry to consider putting more efforts into this.
